title: Customer CRM
summary: Manage companies, contacts, deals, duplicate records, and reliable customer activity history.
outcome: A searchable CRM with relationship-aware CRUD, duplicate resolution, owner-scoped access, and tested data portability.
prerequisites: Project tracker, related milestones, and verified-session CRUD. Create a separate React, Effect API, and PostgreSQL repository.
model: Company: id, ownerId, name, domain, archivedAt. Contact: id, companyId, name, email, revision.
Deal: id, companyId, contactId, stage, valueMinorUnits, currency, revision. Activity: actor, subject, action, time.
Store optional values deliberately. An unknown email is different from a known empty string; money requires an explicit currency and precision policy.
boundaries: React editors → company/contact/deal services → owner-scoped repositories. Relationship changes and their history share a transaction.

milestones.title: Create a company and contact directory
milestones.brief: Ship labeled company and contact editors with optional fields, archived states, and clear relationship validation.
milestones.explanation: A form model is not automatically a persistence model. Normalize display input at a known boundary, preserve meaningful user text, and validate relationships inside the service. Decide whether email and domain are identifiers, hints, or merely attributes; treating every shared domain as one company can accidentally merge unrelated customers.
steps: Define company and contact creation examples, including unknown email, a missing company, and an archived parent. Write the field normalization rules.
Implement owner-scoped list/detail/create/update/archive operations and forms. Keep a contact's identity stable when its company changes.
Test direct API calls, failed writes retaining drafts, reload persistence, and contacts whose parent is archived.

checks.label: Company/contact CRUD persists and enforces declared relationships.
Optional values keep their documented meaning across form and API.
Another owner cannot read or modify the directory.

milestones.stretch: Add a contact move operation with an activity entry that preserves the original relationship in history.

milestones.title: Model deal stages and amounts
milestones.brief: Add deals with a controlled stage workflow and money values that survive round trips without floating-point surprises.
milestones.explanation: A pipeline stage is a business state, not an arbitrary label. Specify allowed transitions and the effect of closing or reopening a deal. Represent amounts using a declared integer-minor-unit or decimal policy and keep currency explicit. Do not aggregate amounts from different currencies as though they were interchangeable.
steps: Write a stage transition table and amount fixtures such as zero, a fractional input, and two currencies. Define required fields for closing a deal.
Implement transition commands and amount decoding at the service boundary. Keep rejected transitions from writing activity events.
Build a pipeline list with accessible move controls and a conflict response for stale revisions. Verify formatting independently of stored arithmetic.

checks.label: Amounts and currencies round-trip according to the precision policy.
Stale moves preserve the user's intended action for review.

milestones.experiment: Submit a close action from two tabs with different amounts and the same revision. Inspect the winning record and ensure the losing draft remains visible.
milestones.review: Check that display formatting is not reused as a database value. Require the agent to explain why its numeric representation matches the supported currencies.
milestones.stretch: Add stage duration metrics using recorded transition times rather than the current record's updatedAt field.

milestones.title: Merge duplicate contacts deliberately
milestones.brief: Preview and confirm a duplicate-contact merge while preserving linked deals and a record of the decision.
milestones.explanation: A suspected duplicate is a suggestion, not proof. Define field conflict resolution, the surviving identity, and reassignment of relationships before committing a merge. Search-based similarity should never silently combine people. A merge transaction must protect the source revisions so its preview cannot overwrite intervening edits.
steps: Create duplicate candidates with conflicting names, emails, and linked deals. Design a field-by-field preview and a stable surviving ID.
Reassign allowed relationships and archive the source record in one transaction, recording who approved the merge. Revalidate revisions at confirmation.
Test a moved deal, a source edited after preview, an inaccessible candidate, and a failure after the first relationship update.

checks.label: Merge decisions are explicit and linked records retain valid ownership.
A failed merge leaves both contacts and relationships unchanged.
Stale previews are rejected or refreshed before applying changes.

milestones.experiment: Preview a merge, attach a new deal to the source, then confirm. Verify the transaction either includes the new relationship safely or requests a new preview.
milestones.review: Explain which information is retained, replaced, or archived. A count of merged rows alone cannot establish that customer context was preserved.
milestones.stretch: Design a reversible merge receipt and identify changes that make automatic undo unsafe.

milestones.title: Search and paginate a growing directory
milestones.brief: Find contacts across companies without leaking other owners' data or issuing a query for every result row.
milestones.explanation: Search semantics need examples: prefix versus substring, case folding, accents, and empty input. Apply authorization before returning totals or suggestions. Stable pagination requires a deterministic ordering and tie-breaker; a cursor is part of the API contract and must be validated like any other unknown input.
steps: Define realistic search fixtures with repeated names, accents, archived records, and two owners. Specify sort order and page-size limits.
Implement a bounded query with company display data and a stable cursor. Inspect the query plan on representative synthetic records.
Test filter changes between requests, malformed cursors, equal sort values, and insertions while paging. Record database query count.

checks.label: Search behavior matches the documented text rules.
Results, counts, and suggestions stay inside the caller's scope.
Pagination and query count remain predictable as data grows.

milestones.experiment: Give an outsider a name fragment that appears only in another owner's records. Verify that result counts and autocomplete do not confirm the hidden contact's existence.
milestones.review: Measure before proposing an index. Include the filter predicates and sort direction in the reasoning so the chosen index actually serves the query.
milestones.stretch: Add saved searches with validated filter schemas and a migration policy for renamed fields.

milestones.title: Build an activity feed with provenance

milestones.explanation: An activity feed can be generated from accepted domain events or inferred from current rows. Inference loses history, so record the facts needed to explain important changes at commit time. Keep the event's display text separate from its structured fields so wording can improve without rewriting historical meaning.
steps: Choose events for contact moves, deal transitions, merges, and archival. Define actor identity, subject references, and visibility rules.
Commit events with their corresponding mutations and render a paginated feed. Handle actors or subjects that later become unavailable.
Test failed commands, repeated requests, identical timestamps, and an archived company. Verify ordering with an explicit secondary key.

checks.label: Only committed changes appear as successful activity.
Each event identifies the verified actor and affected subject.
Deleted or archived references do not break the timeline.

milestones.experiment: Retry a command after its response is lost. Confirm the same business action does not create two misleading activity events.
milestones.review: Separate a useful activity feed from compliance claims. Document what events are intentionally omitted and which roles may read historical details.
milestones.stretch: Add a filtered company timeline without duplicating the same event into multiple stores.

milestones.title: Export, archive, and restore customer data
milestones.brief: Finish the CRM with a scoped export and a tested restore that preserves relationships and activity meaning.
milestones.explanation: Data portability is a workflow with access control, a format contract, and a recovery procedure. Define which archived rows and activity references are included. Deletion, archival, and redaction are distinct product choices; choose a policy with stakeholders instead of assuming one button can satisfy every retention requirement.
steps: Create a small export containing related companies, contacts, deals, currencies, and activities. Document identifiers and unsupported format versions.
Authorize and bound the export, then restore into an independent empty database. Verify relationships before making imported data visible.
Rehearse an archival or redaction request under a stated sample policy and inspect search, exports, caches, and timeline rendering afterward.

checks.label: Exports contain only authorized records and required relationships.
A restored CRM supports the same create/search/deal workflow.
Lifecycle actions behave consistently across lists, feeds, and exports.
